title: kvcache shard eviction hysteresis and poison-probe implementation
creator: Asha Raman
description: Follow-up actions and engineering plan after the 2026-01-28 prefix cache capacity event. The incident manifested as periodic shard-level eviction storms that caused throughput drops and a small class of stale-pointer reads leading to request errors under specific allocation patterns. This ticket coordinates a multi-pronged fix: add eviction hysteresis per-shard, introduce lightweight poison-probe sweeps to detect contamination windows, and harden pointer stability checks + telemetry to surface regressions early.
background_and_symptoms: On 2026-01-28 we observed recurring throughput degradation correlated with bursts of eviction activity in kvcache shards.
Symptoms: transient 5-15% tail latency regressions, elevated 5xxs during shard compaction windows, and memory growth in nodes with uneven namespace distribution.
Existing mitigations (emergency): temporary eviction-rate throttles and increasing slab reservation for hot namespaces; both are stopgaps and increased overall memory footprint.
timeline_summary: 2026-01-28 02:12 UTC: First alert from SLOs (p95 latency) and cache eviction rate spike.
2026-01-28 03:05 UTC: Oncall rolled out eviction-rate throttle (hotfix) which reduced immediate tail latency but increased memory pressure.
2026-02-02: Initial RCA drafted; pointed to oscillation between aggressive shard-level eviction and concurrent prefetch operations that created transient stale pointers.
2026-02-10: This ticket opened to implement longer-term safeguards and detection.
root_cause: A combination of aggressive cross-shard prefetching heuristics and a reactive global eviction policy caused repeated eviction waves. Evictions raced with async compaction and iterator reads, producing windows where pointer references to just-freed slab segments were observed. The runtime lacked a short-lived contamination detection signal to abort reads when pointer stability could not be guaranteed.
proposed_solution_overview: Implement per-shard eviction hysteresis to prevent oscillation, add a lightweight 'poison-probe' background sweep that marks recently-evicted regions for a short quarantine window, and add deterministic pointer-stability checksums to detect corrupted references in debug builds. Complement with telemetry: shard eviction score distributions, quarantine occupancy, and a 'contamination_event' trace.
acceptance_criteria: No repeat of eviction storm oscillation in synthetic workload reproductions (1000 QPS mixed workload) for 24h.
Repro test suites that previously triggered stale-pointer reads fail no longer with the new quarantine/probe enabled.
Telemetry dashboards for shard hysteresis and contamination events present in Console and have alerting thresholds.
Rollout plan documented with automatic rollback criteria and canary verification steps.
implementation_tasks: ENG: add per-shard hysteresis parameters (min-eviction-interval, hysteresis-factor) behind runtime flags - owner: Miguel
ENG: implement poison-probe sweep (configurable quarantine TTL per-shard) that marks freed slabs for short window - owner: Priya
ENG: add optional deterministic pointer-stability checksum in debug builds to catch invalid references - owner: Yuki
ENG: extend telemetry (metrics + traces) and add contamination_event log line - owner: Sam
ENG: write unit + integration tests (race conditions, synthetic stress harness) - owner: Miguel & Priya
SRE: add dashboard panels, alert rules, and runbook edits - owner: Jordan
QA: run 24h resiliency soak with real traffic replay and measure p95/p99 latency - owner: QA team
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hysteresis tuned too conservatively could delay needed evictions and increase memory usage. Mitigation: expose flags and staging-only defaults; run controlled soak tests and set memory budget alarms.
Risk: Poison-probe adds CPU overhead during sweeps. Mitigation: make sweeps incremental, shard-local, and rate-limited; measure CPU and adjust TTL.
Risk: Pointer-checksum overhead in release builds. Mitigation: checksum only enabled in debug/e2e builds and a lightweight CRC variant when enabled in canary clusters.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flags behind runtime-flags gate; land in main branch.
2) Enable on internal staging clusters with low traffic; validate synthetic tests and telemetry.
3) Canary rollout to 5% of capacity in us-west-2 for 48h; monitor contamination_event, eviction-rate, p95.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% with automated rollback if contamination_event > 1/min or p95 regression > 10%.
5) Full rollout after 7-day observation and sign-off from SRE and Product.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: New alert: contamination_event rate > 0.5/min for 10m -> Pager (sev2)
Dashboard: eviction-score heatmap per-shard + quarantine occupancy timeseries.
testing_plan: Unit tests for hysteresis parameter boundary conditions and correct fallback behavior.
Integration: synthetic mixed workload harness reproducing previous oscillation pattern; expect no oscillation for 24h.
Chaos: simulate shard compaction and concurrent iterators under high allocation churn in staging environment.
Performance: measure CPU and memory delta with poison-probe enabled, target <2% CPU overhead at baseline QPS.
post_release_checks: Verify canary metrics and runbook threshold checks at 1h, 6h, 24h after each rollout phase.
Collect and review contamination_event traces for false positives and adjust TTL/hysteresis accordingly.
Run cost analysis for memory footprint change and present to Product with recommendations.
notes: This approach favors availability and predictable throughput over minimal memory footprint; product trade-off required (see label 'memory-ops').
Discussed alternative: fully lock-step compaction (too high latency). Decided against due to impact on throughput.
We will coordinate release window with Dedicated infra team to avoid overlapping cluster upgrades.
